name: the Great Court
description: The terraced court at the heart of the University, where every path crosses. The bell that rings the lecture hours hangs here, beside the board where notices are nailed.

name: the Lecture Halls
description: The open pavilions and stone halls where the colleges teach. Students sit on tiered benches; the lecturer reads from the table in the middle.

name: the Chained Library
description: A cold stone library where the valuable books are chained to the shelves and the reading cells are lit by oil lamps.

name: the Student Commons
description: The refectory and common room: long tables, a great hearth, cheap stew, and somewhere warm to sit when the lectures are over.

name: the Furrow Chapel
description: The College of Divinity's chapel of the First Furrow, open to any student who wants quiet or counsel.

name: the Tiltyard
description: The University's sports ground: a sanded ring with stands for bouts and games, archery butts, and the drill yard where the Cadet Watch trains at dawn.

name: the Physic Garden
description: The walled garden of the College of Husbandry and Herbcraft: raised beds of herbs and vegetables, bean poles, and a still pond at the far end.

name: the Bathhouse
description: The students' communal baths: a warm tiled pool under a vaulted roof, fed from the hot spring the University was built over.

name: the Cloister Halls
description: The student dormitories: timbered halls around a cloister, two beds to a room under the rafters, a porter at the gate after dark. Your own room is here.

name: Lantern Row
description: The street outside the University gate where students who can afford it rent rooms above the shops, away from the porters and the curfew.

name: the Honeyed Bee Inn
description: The inn on Lantern Row where half the University drinks: card games, strong ale, and rooms upstairs.

name: the Market Square
description: Seedblossom's market, a short walk from the gate: a sea of awnings where students find work, supplies and gossip.

name: Dawnbloom House
description: The crown's white marble house in a walled garden at the north-east corner of the grounds. The Chancellor receives guests here, and by custom the heir to the throne lodges in it during term.
